payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #675 (recipes add in a folder repository made it a recipe library, so every default silently left .brokkr/ for .forge/). OPERATOR RULING on #675, 2026-10-15: option A. `recipes add` refuses in a folder repository, names the folder, and writes nothing; in a recipe library or a bare repository it behaves exactly as before. The issue's acceptance stands. On 2026-10-15 the operator ACCEPTED, for this PR (recorded on #675): the three refusal texts quoted in item 5(a) as built; the two behaviour changes in 5(b) and 5(c); and the union reading in 5(d). They are rulings now, not open questions: name them in the PR as accepted, and do not return the branch over them.

The branch story-675-recipes-add-folder ends at ba08f7b7. It was cut from #634 slice B's head 47eb47a3 because slice B rewrote the verb this story changes; slice B merged to main as 5caf84d7 (#686), and 7ffb1c8e merges that main into this branch. Its one conflict, in tests/init_doctor.rs's the_recipe_verbs_read_the_provisional_offices_the_map_lists, takes this branch's side; main's other init_doctor hunk (slice B's macOS fix 443d8385: the unpinned-model test's inline sites drop `hands`, because init declares the `harness` boundary on macOS) merges cleanly. The branch's diff against main is exactly 47eb47a3..42d6328b, line for line.
- 1dc5f277 (story run implement-story-675-recipes-add--a5f143ee): recipes::add calls refuse_folder before it clones, copies or creates anything. refuse_folder walks places::Layout::discover from the workspace and from the nearest standing ancestor of absolute(--dir), and refuses recipes::InFolder { root } when either walk finds Kind::Folder. tests/init_doctor.rs (a slice-B file) has one hunk: its add step ran inside a folder repository and now asserts the refusal, planting the library through machine_proof::copy_dir (made pub(crate)). Its review returned a SECURITY-HOLD: `--dir missing/../<repo>/recipes` from outside was judged lexically, from the wrong place.
- cc5b92eb (fix round fix-round-675b-for-story-675-rec-9ac384d5, first visit): add refuses Unplain::Name for a --name that is not one plain path component, before anything is read or written; refuse_folder refuses Unplain::Dir when the part of absolute(--dir) below its nearest standing entry holds any component that is not plain, before both walks. One fn plain() is the rule behind base_of and both checks. add's git clone block moved unchanged into fn clone so add stays at CC 15.
- 42d6328b (fix round, second visit, answering its review's MEDIUM): plain() judges the spelling itself (not empty, not '.' or '..', no separator byte), so --name 'x/', 'x//', 'x/.' and 'x/./' refuse as Unplain::Name before anything is written.
- 7ffb1c8e: the controller's merge of main 5caf84d7 (above).
- The first landing (landing-pr-for-story-675-recipes-c885bc2b) judged 7ffb1c8e and returned a SECURITY-HOLD: refuse_folder judged --dir as it canonicalizes, so <repo>/recipes as a link outward, or as a nested git repository (a submodule's shape), installed from outside and flipped the journal to .forge/forge.db. Every other item held.
- c54c6380 (fix round fix-round-675c-for-story-675-rec-9b73561a): refuse_folder also judges every standing lexical ancestor of absolute(--dir), as spelled, through places::Layout::discover; recipes.rs's restated `fn unreadable` (a copy of places.rs's private helper) is inlined. Its review held those two shapes closed and returned a SECURITY-HOLD on a third: an outside link to a nested repository at <repo>/recipes (`--dir alias`).
- ba08f7b7 (fix round fix-round-675d-for-story-675-rec-b889c76e): the walk also takes every ancestor of the real directory `at` resolves to (Layout::cwd() of the one judgement, no second canonicalize), de-duplicated against the spelled walk, through one extracted function refuse_any; refuse_folder is CC 6 and add stays at 15. Its review ruled residual at LOW with no security residual, and its chief wrote the class argument: the mark lands at canonical(at)/<rest>/<name>/bundle.json with <rest> plain and absent, so a folder repository R that would see it as <R>/recipes/<name>/bundle.json is canonical(at) or one of its ancestors, each judged at its own nearest .git.
Host exact coverage (100% lines, branches and functions) and every host lint and ratchet, complexity included, are green on ba08f7b7. (The first coverage attempt failed one broker timing test this branch does not touch, broker::rpc::tests::a_cancellation_behind_an_answer_the_harness_leaves_untaken_settles_in_two_seconds at 3.03s against [2s, 3s); the rerun was green.)

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, reproducing each on the HEAD binary (build it; a folder repository is `git init` then `brokkr init .`):
1. #675's acceptance: in a folder repository, `recipes add <local bundle> --name x` refuses with the exact InFolder text from the root, from a subdirectory (default --dir), from a bare directory outside with `--dir <repo>/recipes`, and from the root with `--dir .brokkr/recipes`. Each writes nothing: no recipes/ directory, the tree under .brokkr/ byte-identical, and `brokkr runs` still reads .brokkr/state/forge.db. In a recipe library (recipes/*/bundle.json) and a bare repository, add installs exactly as on main. `recipes list` and `recipes show` are unchanged in every layout.
2. The place judged is the place written, for every shape the three security holds named: from a bare P outside, with --dir naming <repo>/recipes where recipes/ is (i) a plain directory, (ii) a link to a directory outside, (iii) a nested `git init` repository, and with (iv) an outside link P/alias -> <repo>/recipes (a nested repository) used as --dir alias, alias/sub and, from a sibling bare repository, ../alias: each refuses with the exact InFolder text naming <repo>, writes nothing under <repo>/recipes or through any link, and leaves `brokkr runs` in <repo> reading .brokkr/state/forge.db. Check the chief's class argument above and look for a shape built from links, nested repositories and `..` that defeats both walks, other than the one carried in 5(i). Also: `--dir missing/../<repo>/recipes` from outside refuses as Unplain::Dir and creates neither <outside>/missing nor <repo>/recipes; `--name ../../<repo>/recipes/x` from a sibling library, with <repo>/recipes/ present and empty, refuses as Unplain::Name and leaves it empty. Look for any other path add writes before its refusals can fire.
3. Tests bind by type (decision 0071 ruling 8) and by exact (code, stderr); the removal controls recorded in the three commits hold.
4. Scope: crates/brokkr-cli/src/recipes.rs, src/recipes/tests.rs, tests/recipes.rs, tests/init_doctor.rs (the one hunk above) and tests/machine_proof.rs (copy_dir's visibility) only. No brokkr-runtime file changes (places.rs is untouched). No public API item moves in any crate, no help text changes (docs/reference/cli.md is untouched), and nothing under contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ changes. Check that 7ffb1c8e (the merge) adds nothing to the diff against main beyond the three commits listed above.
5. For the PR, name each as information, none returning the branch: (a) the three refusal texts, quoted exactly; (b) `--dir ""` now refuses as PlacesError::Unreadable where it once installed into the working directory (a degenerate input); (c) base_of now judges an `extends` by its spelling, so a value spelled 'base/' plans no copy and the strict compile names why the layer does not compose; (d) the refusal reads EITHER the working directory's layout OR --dir's (the union), so from inside a folder repository even a --dir outside it refuses; the operator may narrow it to the destination alone; (e) carried, pre-existing: create_dir_all(dir) runs before the source is checked, so an empty library directory is left when the source is not a directory, the clone fails or the compile refuses (now only outside folder repositories); (f) LOW: a race between the judgement and create_dir_all is a deliberate evasion under the 2026-09-26 threat model; (g) the workspace layout is walked twice per add, one judgement called twice; (h) standing()'s unwrap_or(Ok(path)) fallback and refuse_folder's strip_prefix expect are invariant guards the exact gate counts as covered; (i) LOW, for the OPERATOR: a folder repository R whose OWN recipes/ is a link outward to E, with --dir naming E directly from outside R, installs E/x and flips R's journal to .forge/forge.db. No walk from --dir reaches R; closing it is a layout-rule change (places::library judging recipes/ as the entry itself, never through a link, as places::folder judges .brokkr) under decision 0083 ruling 4, the operator's to open. It is a property of the layout rule on main, not a refusal this diff weakens; (j) the union reading's over-refusals, named in c54c6380: a git recipe library nested inside a folder repository, link or `..` spellings under a folder whose mark would land outside it, and a non-repository ancestor holding .brokkr; (k) pre-existing on main: the Unreadable text for a dangling --dir prints its io source twice (PlacesError's Display plus anyhow's chain).
Out of this PR's scope, by the operator's word, and NOT a finding against it: doctor from a subdirectory of a recipe library creating <cwd>/.forge/forge.db (carried from #634 slice B, already on main); #634 slice C's work (guides, doc_truth, R5, places::Layout::of_root).

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib recipes::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it -- recipes:: brokkr_folder:: init_doctor:: suppressions::; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. If a suppression changes, say so: the controller regenerates quality/suppressions.txt. A new test file is named *_tests.rs or tests.rs. If no finding is in this run's scope, report the run complete with the carried items in notes, rather than blocked.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
